_note: This is the game's DEFAULT style — used for room backgrounds and in-room character sprites. Cutscene-only portrait art bypasses this file with hand-written prompts. History in one day: (1) close-up cinematic-portrait camera used for rooms by mistake — looked like a photo backdrop with cutouts standing in front; (2) fixed the camera angle but kept painterly/vignette rendering — still murky/unreadable, user said 'think Stardew Valley'; (3) went fully flat/clean/cel-shaded Stardew — user then said this 'doesn't fit the bill... just looks like stardew' and pointed back at the actual inspiration images (reference/the-game/inspo-*.png) and the already-generated character portraits (e.g. michael.png) as the real target: both are richly saturated, moody, warm-vs-cool lit, and textured — nothing like flat Stardew cel-shading. This version keeps ONLY the structural lessons that were actually validated as correct (top-down orthogonal camera, real floor plane, fixed door position) and reverts the rendering technique back toward the game's actual established look.
camera: Top-down RPG interior room view: a clean, gently-angled overhead perspective, orthogonal walls, a clearly readable rectangular floor plane. NEVER an eye-level photograph, NEVER a close-up character-portrait crop. IF the room has a door/archway leading elsewhere: it MUST be positioned on the back-right wall, appearing in roughly the rightmost 15-20% of the frame width, with its threshold at floor level (not floating high on the wall) — this exact position is hardcoded as the walkable exit trigger in the game engine, so a door drawn anywhere else means players can see a door they can't actually use. The walkable floor must begin no higher than roughly 45-48% down the frame — furniture/counters/shelving above that line, open floor below it.
style: Detailed 16-bit pixel art matching this game's own established look (see reference/the-game/inspo-*.png and the character portraits already generated, e.g. michael.png, kat.png) — NOT Stardew Valley's flat cel-shading. Rich, saturated color with real depth: warm light sources (lanterns, windows, candles) casting an actual warm glow against cooler ambient walls/shadow, visible texture on surfaces (brick coursing, wood grain, fabric folds), confident dark outlines. Still requires clean, sharply readable orthogonal architecture — walls meet the floor at a clear line, furniture silhouettes are unambiguous — richness of color/lighting must never come at the cost of the room reading as a coherent walkable space. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: same rich rendering technique and palette as the portrait busts, at a small full-body top-down scale, head-to-feet, clean readable silhouette from the overhead angle.
palette: Saturated, warm-vs-cool contrast — warm amber/gold light pooling against cooler blue, indigo, or wood-brown ambient tone, matching the inspiration images (e.g. inspo-08's warm doorway/window glow against cool blue brick walls). Not evenly lit throughout — real light sources create real pools of brighter warm light against a moodier surrounding tone, as long as the overall room still reads clearly (no area so dark the architecture becomes ambiguous).
background: For a ROOM: a complete, atmospherically-lit top-down interior appropriate to the space, empty of any characters or people, with an unmistakable open floor area filling most of the lower frame. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: isolated on a transparent background, no scene/ground/shadow drawn in.
constraints: No text, no logos, no watermark, no UI elements, no borders/frames baked into the image. A room must have clean orthogonal architecture (walls meet the floor at a clear, readable line) — reject anything where the walls or furniture look melted, warped, or spatially incoherent, but rich atmospheric lighting/color is expected and desired, not a flaw. STRICTLY no people/characters/figures anywhere in a room background — confirmed failure mode: a stray character rendered standing in the scene despite this. A character sprite must be full body head-to-feet, standing, facing toward the viewer — never a close-up bust/portrait crop. CRITICAL for any character sprite (not a room background): isolated ONLY on a plain transparent background — absolutely no scene, room, walls, furniture, or floor drawn in, just the character alone. Any character wearing glasses must have clearly visible human eyes — pupils and eye whites — showing behind the lenses, never blank/hidden skin tone.
